Invoke the call under test (e.g. token refresh)

The final call succeeds and its response is returned

budget.target: outbound Keycloak call: max 2 retries, 5s timeout/attempt, ~250ms exponential backoff base with jitter
budget.measured: exactly 3 total attempts (1 initial + 2 retries) observed; each attempt configured with 5s timeout; backoff followed the pinned exponential formula (0.25s, 0.5s) verified via monkeypatched sleep calls

Outbound HTTP client spied to count calls
steps: Mock Keycloak's refresh endpoint to return 400 on every call
Spy on the outbound HTTP client's call count
POST /auth/refresh with a refresh_token
expected_results: Outbound call spy recorded exactly 1 call
Response status is 401 (per FR-6), returned without a retry delay

test_cases.title: Access/refresh token values never appear in log output; only user_id is logged
test_cases.given: a successful callback and a successful refresh, each producing real token values
test_cases.when: log output for both requests is captured
test_cases.then: no captured log line contains the literal access_token or refresh_token value; only user_id appears among identity-bearing fields
test_cases.objective: Verify NFR-4's PII/token-logging prohibition end-to-end across both trigger points.
preconditions: Keycloak mocked to return known token values on callback and on refresh
stdout log capture enabled for both requests
steps: Mock Keycloak to return test_data token values on callback and on refresh
GET /auth/callback and POST /auth/refresh, each with log capture enabled
Search all captured log lines for the literal token substring values
expected_results: Neither token value appears anywhere in captured log output
Only user_id appears among identity fields in the dashboard_login log entries

test_cases.title: A client-supplied role/group header is ignored; role and groups come only from the validated JWT
test_cases.given: a validly signed JWT with role 'qa' and groups ['program-beta'], plus a forged X-Role/X-Groups request header claiming role 'admin' and groups ['program-alpha']
test_cases.when: the shared auth dependency derives the session
test_cases.then: the derived role and groups come only from the JWT claims; the forged header is ignored entirely
test_cases.objective: Verify the server-side RBAC foundation: role/groups are sourced exclusively from the validated JWT, never a client-supplied header, at the point this story controls (full RBAC enforcement is AUTH-03, out of scope here).
preconditions: JWKS mocked to serve the signing key for the test JWT
steps: Build a JWT with role 'qa' and groups ['program-beta']
Call a protected test route with Authorization: Bearer <jwt> plus the forged X-Role/X-Groups headers
Inspect the derived session
expected_results: session.role == 'qa' (not 'admin')
session.groups/program-membership derives only from the JWT's groups claim, not the forged header

test_cases.title: AUTH-01 exposes no HTML sign-in surface; the accessibility budget is honestly out of scope at the backend layer
test_cases.given: the full set of routes AUTH-01 registers (/auth/login, /auth/callback, /auth/refresh, /auth/dev-bypass)
test_cases.when: each route's response media type is inspected
test_cases.then: none render text/html or any sign-in page markup — all are JSON API responses or redirects
test_cases.objective: Confirm NFR-6's 'N/A — WCAG AA owned by SHP-01's frontend sign-in page' claim is structurally true for this story's routes, not just asserted in prose.
preconditions: Full route table introspectable via app.routes
steps: Enumerate AUTH-01's registered routes via app.routes
For each route, issue a representative request and inspect Content-Type / response shape
expected_results: No route returns Content-Type: text/html
No route serves rendered page markup — only JSON bodies or redirect responses with no HTML template involved

test_cases.title: All /auth/* routes emit structlog JSON-formatted log output
test_cases.given: requests to each /auth/* route
test_cases.when: log output is captured for a request to each route
test_cases.then: every emitted log line is valid structured JSON (app/core/logging.py's structlog formatter), not a plain-text/unstructured line
test_cases.objective: Verify NFR-7's general JSON-output requirement across all /auth/* routes, distinct from FR-10's specific dashboard_login trigger/field-scope check.
preconditions: stdout log capture enabled
steps: For each route in test_data.routes, issue a representative request with log capture enabled
Attempt to json.loads() every captured log line
expected_results: Every captured log line for every /auth/* route parses as valid JSON
No unstructured plain-text log line is emitted for any /auth/* request

test_cases.title: Callback's expires_in passes through Keycloak's real value unmodified, never hardcoded to the 300s test-fixture default
test_cases.given: Keycloak's token endpoint returns expires_in=600 (deliberately not the Apexon realm's documented 300s default)
test_cases.when: the callback route returns its JSON body
test_cases.then: expires_in in the response equals 600, proving the value is realm-driven and never a hardcoded 300s constant
test_cases.objective: Verify the access-token lifetime is realm-driven per NFR-8, not a pinned code constant.
preconditions: Keycloak token endpoint mocked to return expires_in=600
steps: Mock Keycloak's token endpoint to return expires_in=600 alongside access_token/refresh_token
GET /auth/callback?code=test-auth-code-1
Inspect the response body's expires_in field
expected_results: Response expires_in == 600, not 300
No code path overwrites or defaults expires_in to a fixed constant

test_cases.title: ENVIRONMENT='staging' is not allow-listed, so dev-bypass is unreachable
test_cases.given: ENVIRONMENT is set to 'staging' — a real deployed environment that is neither production nor a member of the non-production allow-list
test_cases.when: the dev-bypass path is invoked
test_cases.then: dev-bypass is unreachable, because the gate grants on allow-list membership rather than denying on equality with 'production'
test_cases.objective: Verify the fail-closed gate refuses a legitimate non-production environment that is not allow-listed. Under the superseded `!= "production"` deny-check this returned a usable token on staging; under FR-1's allow-list it does not (Product Gate decision 2026-08-27).
preconditions: Test app booted with ENVIRONMENT=staging
steps: Boot the test app with ENVIRONMENT=staging
Read the normalized Settings.environment
POST /auth/dev-bypass with a role/email/programs override
expected_results: Settings normalizes environment to 'staging'
'staging' is not a member of {local, development, dev, test, ci}
Response status is 404
No access_token or refresh_token is present anywhere in the response body

test_cases.title: An unrecognized ENVIRONMENT value (typo) fails closed rather than enabling dev-bypass
test_cases.given: ENVIRONMENT is set to 'produciton' — a misspelling of 'production', the realistic deployment accident this gate must survive
test_cases.when: the dev-bypass path is invoked
test_cases.then: dev-bypass is unreachable, because an unrecognized value is not a member of the non-production allow-list
test_cases.objective: Verify the sole security gate fails closed on an unanticipated value. A `!= "production"` deny-check treats every typo as non-production and would serve dev-bypass tokens from a production deployment; allow-list membership inverts that default (research condition C-4, Product Gate decision 2026-08-27).
preconditions: Test app booted with ENVIRONMENT=produciton
steps: Boot the test app with ENVIRONMENT=produciton
Read the normalized Settings.environment
POST /auth/dev-bypass with a role/email/programs override
expected_results: Settings normalizes environment to 'produciton'
'produciton' is not a member of {local, development, dev, test, ci}
Response status is 404
No access_token or refresh_token is present anywhere in the response body

test_cases.title: Every allow-listed non-production ENVIRONMENT value keeps dev-bypass reachable
test_cases.given: ENVIRONMENT is set to each member of the non-production allow-list in turn
test_cases.when: the dev-bypass path is invoked
test_cases.then: dev-bypass issues a bearer token for every allow-listed value, so fail-closed gating does not break local or CI development
test_cases.objective: Verify the allow-list is complete enough to serve its purpose — the fail-closed gate must not lock developers or CI out of dev-bypass. Guards against over-tightening FR-1's allow-list (AC-8).
preconditions: Test app booted per the parametrized ENVIRONMENT value
steps: For each value in {local, development, dev, test, ci}: boot the test app with that ENVIRONMENT
POST /auth/dev-bypass with a role/email/programs override
Assert the Keycloak HTTP client spy recorded zero calls for that iteration
expected_results: Response status 200 for all five values
Each response body is shaped {access_token, refresh_token, expires_in} with no Set-Cookie header
Zero outbound Keycloak calls across all five iterations

test_cases.title: A dev-bypass token is accepted by a get_current_user-protected route in an allow-listed environment, and rejected in production
test_cases.given: ENVIRONMENT is an allow-listed non-production value and a token has been obtained from POST /auth/dev-bypass
test_cases.when: that token is presented as Authorization: Bearer on a route guarded by Depends(get_current_user)
test_cases.then: the request is authenticated and the derived role/programs match the dev-bypass overrides; the same token is rejected with 401 when the app is built with ENVIRONMENT=production
test_cases.objective: Close the AF-05 gap: prove dev-bypass delivers the story's stated outcome (local sign-in without a live IdP) end-to-end, and that D-08's ephemeral dev signing key is served ONLY under the D-01 fail-closed allow-list.
preconditions: App built via create_app with an allow-listed ENVIRONMENT
No Keycloak JWKS endpoint reachable or mocked — dev-bypass must not depend on one
steps: POST /auth/dev-bypass with the role/email/programs overrides
Present the returned access_token as Authorization: Bearer on a get_current_user-protected route
Assert the derived CurrentUser matches the overrides
Rebuild the app with ENVIRONMENT=production and present the same token to the guarded route
expected_results: Guarded route returns 200 in the allow-listed environment
Derived role == 'qa' and programs == ['alpha']
No outbound Keycloak call is made at any point
Under ENVIRONMENT=production the same token is rejected 401 (the dev kid is not served by the JWKS cache)

test_cases.title: An expired access token is rejected with 401 on a protected route
test_cases.given: an access token with a valid signature from a recognized kid, but an exp claim in the past
test_cases.when: it is presented as Authorization: Bearer on a route guarded by Depends(get_current_user)
test_cases.then: the request is rejected with 401 through the standard error envelope, indistinguishable from any other rejection reason
test_cases.objective: Pin expiry enforcement. authlib's jwt.decode() checks only the signature; only claims.validate() checks exp — an implementation missing that call passes every other test case and accepts expired tokens indefinitely.
preconditions: JWKS mocked to serve the signing key so signature verification genuinely succeeds
steps: Mint a correctly-signed token with exp 120 seconds in the past
Present it on a get_current_user-protected route
expected_results: Response status is 401
Body matches the standard error envelope with a generic detail
The failure comes from claim validation, not signature verification (the signature is valid)

test_cases.title: A validly-signed token with the wrong issuer or wrong audience is rejected with 401
test_cases.given: a token whose signature verifies against the configured JWKS, but whose `iss` is not the configured OIDC issuer, or whose `aud` does not include the configured OIDC client id
test_cases.when: it is presented as Authorization: Bearer on a route guarded by Depends(get_current_user)
test_cases.then: the request is rejected with 401 through the standard error envelope, indistinguishable from any other rejection reason
test_cases.objective: Close the cross-client confused-deputy gap found by code review (REVIEW.md F-1). authlib's validate_aud()/validate_iss() are NO-OPS unless claims_options is passed to jwt.decode — verified against the installed authlib source and empirically: a token with iss='https://EVIL.example.com' and aud='some-other-client' passed .validate() without raising. Every client in the Apexon realm is signed by the same realm key, so without this check a token minted for a DIFFERENT application in the realm would be accepted here as a valid session.
preconditions: JWKS mocked to serve the signing key so signature verification genuinely SUCCEEDS — the rejection must come from claim validation, not from a bad signature
Settings configured with a known oidc_issuer and oidc_client_id
steps: Mint a correctly-signed token whose iss is the wrong issuer; present it to a guarded route
Mint a correctly-signed token whose aud is a different client id; present it to a guarded route
Mint a correctly-signed token with both correct; present it to a guarded route
Repeat the happy path for a dev-bypass token in an allow-listed environment
expected_results: Wrong issuer -> 401 via the standard error envelope
Wrong audience -> 401 via the standard error envelope
Correct issuer and audience -> 200 (the check must not reject valid tokens)
A dev-bypass token still authenticates in an allow-listed environment (the fix must not break D-08)
